sentences.text:
THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT MFA No.201255/2017 is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Additional District Judge and M.A.C.T. Bidar (henceforth referred to as 'Tribunal') in MVC No.595/2015 vide its common judgment and award dated 17.01.2017.
2. MFA No.200866/2021 is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Tribunal in MVC No.594/2015 vide its common judgment and award dated 17.01.2017.

3. The impugned judgment and award discloses that the claimant in MVC No.594/2015 was taking his mother for treatment and boarded an autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA-32-B-8600 (henceforth referred to as 'offending vehicle').

The driver of the offending vehicle drove it in a rash and negligent manner and lost control and dashed against a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-39-4728 ridden by the NC: 2023:KHC-K:5518 claimant in MVC No.595/2015.

As a result,
mother of the claimant in MVC No.594/2015 suffered injuries and she was shifted to Government Hospital, Mannakhelli, where she was administered first-aid and referred to Government Hospital,
Bidar.
However, she died on the way to the hospital.
He claimed that the deceased was aged 60 years and was earning a sum of Rs.300/- per day by vending milk.
4. The claimant in MVC No.595/2015 claimed that he had suffered injuries in the aforesaid accident.
He claimed that he was dealer of kerosene and was earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
Hence, separate claim petitions were filed by the injured claimant in MVC No.595/2015 and dependant legal heir of Smt. Sangamma, who died in the accident.
5. The insurer contested the claim petitions on various grounds.
It denied the accident as well as the injuries suffered by the claimant in MVC No.595/2015 and the death of Smt. Sangamma in the accident.
It also denied the age, avocation and income of the injured claimant as well as the deceased .
6. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petitions were set down for trial.
The claimant in MVC No.594/2015 was NC: 2023:KHC-K:5518 examined as PW.1 and the injured claimant in MVC No.595/2015 was examined as PW.2.
Exs.P1 to P12 were marked.

A doctor was examined as PW.3 Rajshekar S/O Bhimrao vs Mr.Shankar And Anr on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169111107/

The insurer however did not lead any evidence.
7. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
It also held that the claimant in MVC No.595/2015 had suffered injures on his right knee, cut lacerated wound over the patella right knee and comminuted fracture of right tibia.

It determined the age of the claimant at 46 years and his notional income at a sum of Rs.5,000/- per month and awarded the following compensation :-
 Sl. Particulars Amount  No. (in Rs.)
 1 Injury, pain and sufferings 30,000/-
 2 Loss of future earnings 78,000/-
 3 Towards medical expenses 1,20,000/-
 4 Towards the conveyance and 5,000/-
 nourishment  Total 2,33,000/-

In so far as the compensation to which dependant legal heir of Smt. Sangamma is concerned, the Tribunal considered the age of the deceased as 60 years and her notional income at a sum of Rs.4,500/- per month and deducted 1/3rd towards personal and living expenses and awarded the following compensation:-
 Sl. Particulars Amount  No. (in Rs.)
 1 Loss of dependency 3,24,000/-
 2 Loss of love and affection 5,000/-
 3 Transportation of dead body 10,000/-
 Total 3,39,000/-
The Tribunal directed the insurer of offending vehicle to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realization.
9.
Being not satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimants in both the claim petitions have filed these appeals.

10. The learned counsel for the claimant in MVC No.595/2015 submitted that the injured claimant in MVC NC: 2023:KHC-K:5518 No.595/2015 had suffered three grievous injuries and PW.3 deposed that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 31.19% to the whole body and therefore, the Rajshekar S/O Bhimrao vs Mr.Shankar And Anr on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169111107/

sentences.text: Tribunal must have considered the disability suffered at not less than 10% to 15%.
He contended that that the notional income of the claimant must have been considered at a sum of Rs.8,000/- as is normally done in similar cases.
He further contends that the compensation awarded under the other heads is also meager.
Consequently, he submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal may be enhanced.

11. The learned counsel for the claimant in MVC No.594/2015 submits that the Tribunal considered the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.4,500/-per month while her notional income must have been considered at a sum of Rs.8,000/- per month.
She also contended that the Tribunal failed to award loss of future prospects at 10%.
Consequently, she prays that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal be enhanced.

12. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurer submitted that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal in NC: 2023:KHC-K:5518 the both the cases is just and proper and does not warrant any enhancement.
13. I have considered the learned counsel for the claimants and the learned counsel for the insurer.
I have also perused the records of the Tribunal as well as its judgment and award.
14. The fact that the claimant in MVC No.595/2015 had suffered injuries in the accident that happened on 02.07.2015 is not much in dispute.
It is found from the medical records that the claimant had suffered comminuted fracture of the right tibia and several wounds over the patella of the right knee.
It also discloses that the claimant had undergone surgery to fix the fracture and that his right leg was shortened by 1.5 inch.

Since the claimant is a kerosene dealer and an agriculturist,
the shortening of the leg is a permanent disability that would definitely affect his day to day activities.
Therefore, the assessment of the disability at 10% by the Tribunal warrants interference and deserves to be considered at 15% to the whole body.

The Tribunal committed an error in considering the notional income of the claimant at Rs.5,000/- per month NC: 2023:KHC-K:5518 while in similar circumstances, the notional income is considered at a sum of Rs.8,000/- per month.
15. Consequently, the claimant in MVC No.595/2015 is entitled to enhanced compensation which is re-determined as follows:-

Sl. Particulars Amount  No. (in Rs.)
 1 Pain and suffering 40,000/-
 2 Medical expenses 1,20,000/-

3 Attendant charges, food, 10,000/-
 nourishment and conveyance  charges

4 Loss of income during the period 24,000/-
 of treatment for three months  5 Loss of income due to disability 1,87,200/-
 (8,000 x 12 x 13 x 15%)
 6 Loss of amenities 40,000/-
 Total 4,21,200/-

Since the liability of the insurer is not challenged, it shall pay the aforesaid compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realisation.
19. In view of the above, MFA No.201255/2017 filed by the claimant in MVC No.595/2015 is allowed in part.

The compensation of Rs.2,33,000/- awarded by the Tribunal in MVC No.595/2015 is enhanced to a sum of Rs.4,21,200/-, which is payable by the insurer along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
However, the claimant is not entitled for interest - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5518 for the delayed period of 1235 days in filing the recalling application.

20. The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this Judgment.
21. Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimant in MVC No.595/2015 in any nationalized Bank for a period of three years.
